limitations: One trial per arm/task on three exposed development cases; no general superiority or statistical reliability claim.
Actual preparation charges occur once; each Sol-led route is allocated the full identical Sol preparation cost/time/calls.
PrimaLabs requested medium maps to thinking enabled; no distinct medium effort value is sent.
Sol subscription output cap is requested but not enforced by its SDK adapter; ledger reservation remains conservative.
Writing wall time excludes planning/checks/grade; whole-route process time includes allocated preparation and path audit.
SDK calculated receipt prices and retained ledger settlements are not independently verified provider invoices.
Subscription-normalized Sol costs use USD/M input0.3, output1.2, cacheRead0.006, cacheWrite0.3; other models retain their receipt costs. Ledger settlements are preserved separately.
Reasoning token counts are informational subsets of model output usage and must not be added to output tokens again.
No later model review or behavioral-feedback repair; application and downstream audited delivery differ.
Bounded lookup/plan-contract failures are route outcomes; they do not establish failed writer capability when no writer was dispatched.
No handoff or lifecycle writer ran in any arm. Muse-self produced no dispatched executable plan.
Only calibration supports a matched Muse-versus-MiMo writer comparison; each has one observation and both passed delivery.
The original zero-call MiMo credential block remains preserved. The separate resume adds no new planning and does not re-charge inherited preparation.
No arm achieved three-case audited delivery; these observations do not justify a new optimal whole-workflow configuration.
